newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Two killed, 12 injured in Macau violence.
newsitem.headline: Two killed, 12 injured in Macau violence.

text.p: Shootings, a firebombing and knife-attack left two people dead and 12 wounded in Macau on Tuesday in the latest wave of violence to rock the tiny enclave.
Police said a nurse died after being shot five times and a suspected gangster was killed after a knife attack at a video game parlour.
Police said they shot the man, in his early 20s, after he and a group of knife-wielding men attacked teenaged students in the game parlour. A dozen students were wounded.
The attackers threw two firebombs into the shop as they ran away from the scene. Police opened fire as the attackers fled, killed the suspected gangster, but the rest of the men escaped.
Four students required hospitalisation. The others were released after receiving medical treatment for stab wounds, police said. They gave no further details.
Nearby, a 34-year-old nurse was shot five times inside her car and pronounced dead on arrival at hospital, police said.
Police sources said the killing was carried out "execution style".
A spokesman for Macau police said they did not know the motives behind both attacks and said the cases were not related.
The woman's death brought to 10 the number of murders in Macau this year, compared with 21 for all of 1996.

The small Portuguese-administrated territory has been hit by a crime wave which is believed to be part of a turf war among rival gangs fighting for control of casino loan-sharking business and prostitution, smuggling and protection rackets.
Macau will become a Special Administrative Region of China on December 20, 1999, two years after its near neighbour, Hong Kong reverts to China rule.
